tldr: This is a loose topical cluster, not one event: 19 independent items from Nov 1 to Nov 19 that each cut inference or agent cost at a different layer. Most are arXiv papers; the rest are engineering posts from Google (XLA Serving Engine), Baseten, Microsoft Research, UW and AWS.
whats_new: Two Nov 19 papers target the KV cache again: RoCoKV compresses redundant tokens in long reasoning traces, and TideCache manages the mixed caches of hybrid-attention open-weight models with layer-wise streaming.
why_it_matters: KV-cache memory is the most-attacked bottleneck in this set (6 of 19 items), so cache policy, not raw FLOPs, is where serving cost and long-context agent capacity are being won or lost.

beats.headline: MoE quantization, expert-parallel compression and speculative decoding
beats.summary: Efficiency inside the model and decode loop: fewer bits, less all-to-all traffic, cheaper draft verification.

beats.headline: Shrink what reaches the model: prompts, images and audio
beats.summary: Input reduction across three modalities: prompt compression, VLM cropping plus compression, and chunked long-audio ASR.

beats.headline: Agent-level efficiency: distilled skills, coordinated delegation, token budgets
beats.summary: Cost cuts at the agent layer rather than the serving stack.

beats.headline: Serving stacks: XLA Serving Engine, edge simulation, cross-Region routing
beats.summary: Infrastructure that decides where and on what hardware requests run.

beats.headline: The KV cache becomes the main target
beats.summary: Six papers attack cache memory: intent-aware prefix reuse, verified compression, prefill/decode KV translation, Gemma 4 shared K=V storage, reasoning-trace compression, and hybrid-model cache streaming.

open_questions: Do any of the KV-cache methods (RoCoKV, TideCache, Verify Before You Fetch) land in vLLM, SGLang or another mainstream serving engine?
Does the Gemma 4 store-K=V-once trick ship in a paged serving engine release, and with what measured memory savings?
Does Google publish throughput or latency benchmarks for XLA Serving Engine against vLLM on the same hardware?
Does TokenEconomizer report a token or cost reduction on a public coding-agent benchmark?
take_for_builders: If long-context or reasoning workloads are memory-bound, profile KV-cache size per request before buying GPUs; on Gemma 4 or hybrid-attention models, check whether your serving engine already exploits their cache structure.
